To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed and implemented the first MLST scheme for the SBSEC, and that we combined this MLST scheme with functional assays to unravel the complexity and health risk of the SBSEC in an overarching One-Health approach.
the SBSEC is a complex group of commensal and pathogen bacteria, which are found in the human and animal gut, in blood and in dairy products.

the SBSEC MLST scheme enabled the phylogenetic and epidemiological classification of the SBSEC strains and the identification of strains with high adhesion to host tissues, high survival in simulated gastric juices and reduced NF-κB activation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a MLST scheme to unravel the phylogeny and epidemiology of the SBSEC.
the identification of the most relevant SBSEC lineages for public health.
the identification of the SBSEC strains that are associated with the greatest health risks and with the elucidation of their mechanisms of action.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SBSEC is a complex group of bacteria that is not well understood yet.
SBSEC strains are commensals with a potential to become opportunistic pathogens.

the SBSEC MLST scheme is a valuable tool for the epidemiological and functional analysis of SBSEC and that the results presented here are a valuable starting point for the further characterization of the complex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MLST is a powerful tool for the analysis of the complex SBSEC.
the SBSEC is a complex group of organisms with a wide range of habitats and hosts.
the MLST scheme developed here can be used to classify SBSEC strains into clades and to identify strains of interest for further investigation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SBSEC strains are not all equal and some lineages are more virulent than others.
the SBSEC MLST can be used to unravel the complexity and diversity of this bacterial group and to identify strains with high adhesion and immune evasion capacities.
